procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine visit. November A1c and kidney numbers were fine. Quiet winter, shoveling a little with the long-handled shovel, back complains but holds up. No palpitation spells. No chest pain.
Oncology letter from October reviewed: stable, observation.
Exam: BP as charted. Irregular rhythm, rate controlled. Lungs clear. No edema.
A/P: no changes. INR in range today. Morphine refill, PDMP reviewed. Physical in April.

documents.title: Anticoagulation visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR below range. Thinks he may have missed two doses last week. Take 7.5 mg tonight, then 35 mg/week. Pill box suggested; wife will set it up. Recheck 3 weeks.

documents.title: Cancelled INR check
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Patient called to cancel this morning's INR check, roads icy. Offered later this week; he will come with his April physical instead.

documents.title: Medicare Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Annual wellness visit, age 71.

Interval: oncology February visit stable per patient. No ED visits since last summer's appendectomy. One low INR in February after missed doses; pill box now.

Function: independent in ADLs and IADLs, drives, wife does the finances. No falls. Sleep fine. PHQ-2 0, AUDIT-C 1. Hearing fine, vision fine with glasses.

Exam: BP as charted. Irregularly irregular, rate controlled, no murmur. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Feet: intact protective sensation, palpable pulses. Neuro grossly normal.

Plan: labs today. Vaccines up to date for now; flu and COVID in the fall. Continue current medications. Advance directive on file. Written plan given.

documents.title: Anticoagulation visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range. Pill box working. Continue. Recheck 6 weeks.

documents.title: Scan
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Had my scan with the cancer doctor last week, she says no change again. Just wanted you to know. Also can I get the morphine sent a day early, we're going to the lake on the 1st. Art

documents.title: RE: Scan
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Great news, Art, thanks for letting me know. Your next morphine fill can go in on the 29th so you have it before you leave; I've noted it. Enjoy the lake.

documents.title: Anticoagulation visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range. No bleeding. Continue 35 mg/week. Next check early September.

documents.title: Wife calling: stroke admission
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Wife called from the hospital. Yesterday afternoon while watching TV his left face drooped, his left arm and leg went weak and his speech slurred; she called 911 right away. The ED said it was a stroke. No clot-busting drug because his blood was already thinned on warfarin, and no clot they could pull out. Admitted to the stroke unit. He is talking more clearly this morning, left arm still weak. PCP notified; she will call when discharge is set and we will see him within a week of going home.

documents.title: PCP call back
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called his wife back. Answered her questions about warfarin; the stroke team will decide on blood thinners. Post-discharge visit to be booked.

documents.title: Post-hospital visit, stroke
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Transitional care visit. Discharged 8/5 after a 4-day stay for an ischemic stroke. The discharge summary has not come yet; history from patient and wife and the discharge medication sheet they brought.

Onset 8/1 in the afternoon at home: left face, arm and leg weakness and slurred speech. On warfarin, so no thrombolysis; MRI showed a stroke on the right side of the brain per the sheet. Speech now normal to him and his wife. Left hand clumsy, grip weaker, walking fine. Outpatient PT and OT start this week. No headache, no new symptoms.

Discharge medication sheet: same as before, warfarin, aspirin, atorvastatin 40, metformin, lisinopril, HCTZ, morphine ER. Reconciled; no changes.

Exam: BP as charted. Irregular, rate controlled. Speech clear. Mild left facial asymmetry with smile. Left grip and finger tapping mildly weaker than right, left arm drift absent. Legs full strength. Gait steady.

A/P
- Acute ischemic stroke, right hemisphere, on warfarin, with mild left arm weakness: therapy as arranged; stroke follow-up per neurology; awaiting summary. Reviewed stroke warning signs and calling 911.
- AF on warfarin: INR today; continue.
- HTN, DM2, CAD: unchanged.
- No driving until cleared by neurology; he agreed.
Follow up in 3 months, sooner as needed.

reports.text: Non-contrast CT head. No intracranial hemorrhage. No mass, mass effect or midline shift. Gray-white differentiation preserved. Ventricles and sulci appropriate for age. No acute abnormality.
reports.conclusion: No hemorrhage or other acute intracranial abnormality.

reports.text: MRI brain without contrast. Restricted diffusion in the right cerebral hemisphere consistent with acute infarction. No hemorrhage on susceptibility imaging. No mass effect. Ventricles normal in size.
reports.conclusion: Acute infarct in the right cerebral hemisphere.

documents.title: Hospital discharge summary, stroke service
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
Regional hospital stroke unit. Admitted 08/01/2024, discharged 08/05/2024.

Presentation: 71 year old man with hypertension, diabetes and atrial fibrillation (previously seen by cardiology and several times in the ED) brought in with abrupt left-sided weakness and slurred speech that began two hours before arrival while he was watching television. His wife reported he had been his usual self earlier that day.
Arrival: BP 165/95, HR 88, afebrile. Left facial droop, left arm and leg weakness, dysarthria. NIH Stroke Scale 12.
Non-contrast CT head: no hemorrhage, no acute abnormality.
INR 2.2 on warfarin: thrombolysis not given. CT angiogram head and neck: no large-vessel occlusion, not a thrombectomy candidate.
MRI: acute infarct in the right cerebral hemisphere.

Course: admitted to the stroke unit, telemetry showed atrial fibrillation. Neurologic deficits improved steadily; at discharge mild left arm weakness only, speech normal. Swallow screen passed.
Assessment: acute ischemic stroke, cardioembolic in the setting of atrial fibrillation.
Discharge medications: warfarin (goal INR 2 to 3), aspirin 81 mg, atorvastatin 40 mg, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg, hydrochlorothiazide 25 mg, morphine sulfate ER 30 mg twice daily. NKDA.
Follow-up: PCP in 1 week; outpatient PT/OT; stroke clinic in 3 months.

documents.title: Anticoagulation visit
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range. Wife drove. Left hand getting stronger with OT, he says. No bleeding. Continue 35 mg/week.

documents.title: INR and vaccines
documents.author: RN
documents.body: INR in range. High-dose flu left deltoid, updated COVID right deltoid; firm pressure after each. No reactions during observation.

documents.title: Diabetic eye examination
documents.author: optometry
documents.body: Dilated exam 10/15/2024. Acuity 20/30 both eyes corrected. Visual fields full to confrontation. No diabetic retinopathy. Cataracts mild, not yet affecting function. Return 12 months.

conditions.label: History of stroke without residual deficits

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Three and a half months after his stroke. Finished PT and OT in October. Says the left hand is as good as it ever was; he's back to small projects in the shop. Stroke clinic appointment is next month. He has not been driving.

Exam: BP as charted. Irregular rhythm. Face symmetric, speech normal. Strength 5/5 and equal in arms and legs, fine finger movements equal, no drift. Gait normal.

A/P
- Ischemic stroke August 2024, recovered without residual deficit. Updated to history of stroke.
- AF: warfarin continued, aspirin continued.
- DM2, HTN: A1c and BMP today; no changes.
- Metastatic colon cancer: on observation with oncology.
- Chronic back pain: ER morphine, PDMP reviewed.
- Driving: defer to the stroke clinic next month.
RTC 3 months.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Surveillance CT chest, abdomen and pelvis with contrast. Comparison 06/2024. Right hepatic lobe lesions unchanged. Bilateral small pulmonary nodules unchanged. Ascending colon thickening unchanged. No new lesion. No adenopathy or ascites.

documents.title: Oncology surveillance visit
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Medical oncology, visit 11/12/2024.
Metastatic right colon adenocarcinoma, observation since November 2022. Interval ischemic stroke in August with good recovery. ECOG 1.
CT stable. CEA 7.1, within his recent range.
Plan: continue observation; CT and CEA in 3 to 4 months; port flushes.
